medications.reason: Supply not on unit. Dose was in main pharmacy IV room batch, ground floor (flooded).

medications.frequency: Continuous, titrate to MAP 65 or above

fields.notes: Barcode scanning and electronic MAR down since the 20:04 network outage; charting on the paper downtime MAR printed at hurricane warning. 19:05: told patient's daughter by phone that the 20:00 antibiotic was coming. 20:00: pip-tazo not on 6 West; called main pharmacy, no answer. 20:31: Pharmacist on call phoned ICU charge: 'Your 20:00 pip-tazo for bay 12 was in the batch the main pharmacy IV room on the ground floor was compounding at 19:45. It's under water. The closest stock is the ICU automated cabinet on floor 3, but nobody is on floor 3 now. I can talk a runner through an override.' 20:33: Daughter called the 6 West desk: 'My dad's nurse told me at 7 that his antibiotic was coming. It's 8:30. Did he miss it? Is he getting worse because of the storm?' Told her the charge nurse will call back. 20:00 vitals: T 37.9 °C, HR 104, BP 102/58, MAP 68, RR 22, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC. — Carla V., RN, 6 West (ICU float)

instructorNote: Core inject: the ground-floor flood has caused a missed antibiotic dose for a patient whose septic shock is resolving, and the 02:00 dose has no supply either. Watch for the ICU charge nurse to send a runner by stairs to the floor 3 cabinet using the pharmacist's override, record the actual time given, and reassess early warning score and sepsis signs. Also watch for the CNO to make sure the attending and unit manager disclose the delay to the daughter within 60 minutes, stick to known facts and document it (NUR-EM-07 section 8).
